data.narrative:
Cylib is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Lilian Schwich, Gideon Schwich, and Paul Sabarny. The target has raised €140M+ to date, comprising a €55M Series A round, a €26.1M NRW grant, and a €63.4M BMWE grant. The Climate & Energy sector contains nine identified peers, including five prominent private companies—Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—plus one public comparable (LNZA).

A traditional peer-median valuation approach is not applicable here. Screening for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables within the Climate & Energy universe yielded zero qualifying datapoints, falling below the minimum threshold of three comps required for statistical reliability. The narrow peer set lacks sufficient depth to support median-based triangulation without introducing material distortion from an all-sector median, which would sacrifice sectoral specificity.

The analysis is therefore constrained by data limitations. Reliance on qualitative positioning within the private peer cohort—or on transaction multiples from the broader Climate & Energy landscape—would be necessary to establish a defensible range, but such methods require additional inputs not present in the current dataset. Key uncertainties center on the marginal performance differential between Cylib and its larger-stage competitors and the applicability of public market valuation multiples (LNZA) to a pre-profitability Series A asset. A credible valuation synthesis requires either expanded peer identification or transaction-level data from similar-stage closings.
